_why:
The #29 review's F5: the first cut of the Version History rule had NO test that bit. Scored at the whole suite, three single-edit boundary mutations were green — `version_history_start` returning +1 instead of +2 (the demotion starts one line ABOVE the heading, i.e. F1 shipped as a permanent off-by-one), the same returning +3, and `VH_MARKER` losing its `##` prefix (any document merely MENTIONING the words silences everything from there, and the shared literal corrupts the assembler at the same time). The spec's only boundary row replaced `in_vh` with `return True`, and a maximal mutation tests that a boundary EXISTS, never where it is.

The boundary now delegates to `h_mad_version_history` — `find_anchor` (refuses more than one heading) and `section_bounds` (stops at the next header or `---`, tracks fences) — so these mutations target that delegation rather than a private arithmetic.

REVISED again after a SECOND fresh review, of the fix itself. It found the boundary's fence mask was a hand-rolled copy of `_fence_events` — the scanner `doc-block-exec.design.md` names as the one home for this grammar — missing a ```` wrapper, a `~~~` fence and a trailing-text closer, and reading a four-space-indented literal fence as an opener (which extended the section PAST a real heading, fail-OPEN). Both ends now resolve over `_fence_events`.

TWO PROPERTIES HERE ARE NOT SINGLE-EDIT MUTATABLE and are reported rather than faked: the indented-fence case and the `##Version History` heading-spelling case are both inherent to `_fence_events`' grammar, not to a predicate in this file. Reverting to the naive scanner (the `the-fence-grammar-is-hand-rolled-again` row) does not reproduce either, because a naive line scan also treats an indented fence as prose and also requires the `#` prefix. Their tests are regression guards over a delegation, which is the property that actually matters: if someone re-implements the grammar here, those tests fail.

mutations.name: the-boundary-starts-one-line-above-the-heading
mutations._mechanism: F1 shipped as a permanent off-by-one: the last hard finding before the history is demoted on EVERY document. This is the mutation that was green across the full suite before the adjacency test existed.

mutations.name: the-section-runs-to-end-of-file-again
mutations._mechanism: F2: every `##` section appended after the history — `## Open Questions`, `## Verification` — is silenced wholesale. One heading covering an unbounded tail is a far wider silencer than `--allow-historical`, which names one pin.
mutations.find:
for event in events:
        if event.lineno <= first:
mutations.replace:
for event in []:
        if event.lineno <= first:

mutations.name: ambiguity-is-resolved-by-taking-the-first-heading
mutations._mechanism: F2: `find_anchor` refuses two headings because for a document carrying a TEMPLATE history above its live one, first-match is the template — and everything between them is the document body. Taking the first silences exactly that span.

mutations.name: the-fence-grammar-is-hand-rolled-again
mutations._mechanism: The pre-fix scanner, restored: no fence grammar at all, so a `## Version History` QUOTED inside any fence anchors a section and silences the body below it. The shipped fix delegates to `_fence_events`, which `doc-block-exec.design.md` names as the one home for this grammar; a hand-rolled copy missed a ```` wrapper, a `~~~` fence and a trailing-text closer.

mutations.name: the-sha-loop-numbers-lines-the-other-way-again
mutations._mechanism: F1's second half. `scan()` carried two line-numbering bases; `hard()` promoted the sha loop's from a printed number to a VERDICT INPUT. With an exotic break above it, a sha inside the history is placed by the wrong basis and escapes the demotion.

mutations.name: the-operators-L-spelling-is-not-normalised
mutations._mechanism: Normalisation now lives INSIDE `historical_by` and applies to both sides. Dropping it from the document's span restores the asymmetry: a declaration written one way is ignored WITHOUT AN ERROR against a document written the other. Un-normalising the DOCUMENT's span breaks the direction where the document writes `:L1` and the declaration `:1` — normalising one side still covers the mirror case, which is why the first `test` key here was caught by the wrong assertion.

mutations.name: a-mixed-spelling-range-parses-as-nothing-again
mutations._mechanism: F10: `L1-L9` and `L1-9` parsed while `1-L9` matched no branch and the span was dropped with NO advisory — silent, and surprising given the help advertises the spellings as interchangeable.

mutations.name: the-normaliser-rewrites-the-whole-token
mutations._mechanism: The over-correction inside `_norm_pin`. Applied to the whole token rather than the tail after the last colon, it turns `src/L1.py:2` into `src/1.py:2` — silencing a pin into a file that does not exist, and doing it to the PATH, which no spelling rule should ever touch.
mutations.find:
head, sep, tail = pin.rpartition(":")
    if not sep or not _LINE_TAIL.match(tail):
        return pin
    return f"{head}:{_line_digits(tail)}"
